title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Entitlement under the Extended Benefits, Trade Readjustment Allowances and Disaster Unemployment Assistance Programs
content:
Extended Benefits (EB), Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA) and Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) entitlements on Unemployment Benefit Claims records are computed differently from regular programs.

## Extended Benefits (EB)

An Extended Benefits claim uses the weekly benefit amount and dependency allowance of its parent claim.

- Retired clause, no longer in force: "the claimant must show the minimum weeks of full-time base-period employment". This clause is superseded by the current basis.
- Retired clause, no longer in force: "its maximum benefit amount is the lesser of the Extended Benefits fraction times the parent claim's maximum benefit amount and the maximum duration weeks times the weekly benefit amount plus dependency allowance." This clause is superseded by the current basis.

## Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA)

1. A Trade Readjustment Allowances claim uses the parent claim's weekly benefit amount plus dependency allowance.
2. Its basic maximum benefit amount is the maximum duration weeks times that weekly amount, less the prior program entitlement, and never below zero. The prior program entitlement is the maximum benefit amount of the parent claim plus the maximum benefit amount of every Extended Benefits claim of the claimant naming the same parent claim.
3. Additional training weeks of Trade Readjustment Allowances are credited by a monetary redetermination only after basic entitlement is exhausted and only while approved training is recorded as enrolled, and the claimant must have enrolled by the training enrollment deadline.

## Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA)

1. A Disaster Unemployment Assistance claim has no wage test. Its weekly benefit amount is computed from the proof of employment or self-employment with the same divisor, is never below the program floor and never above the ceiling.
2. Its maximum benefit amount is the maximum duration weeks times the weekly benefit amount, payable only for weeks inside the disaster assistance period.
3. Proof of employment or self-employment must reach the agency within the proof deadline after filing, or the claim is redetermined at the program floor and any amount paid above the floor becomes an overpayment.
4. A Disaster Unemployment Assistance claim may be filed without good cause only on or before the filing deadline after the disaster declaration announcement. The filing deadline is counted in calendar days starting the day after the disaster declaration announcement, and a claim filed on the last day is timely. With good cause a later claim is accepted until the late filing limit weeks after the announcement, and never after it.

The announcement date read for point 4 is the disaster declaration date recorded on the claim.

### Filing deadline, both sides (a 30-day deadline and a 26-week late filing limit)

| Filing day, counted from the day after the announcement | Without good cause | With good cause |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 through day 30 | Timely | Timely |
| Day 31 up to the 26-week limit after the announcement | Not accepted | Accepted |
| After the 26-week limit | Not accepted | Not accepted |

### Hypothetical figures

- TRA: a parent claim with a maximum benefit amount of 9000.00 and one Extended Benefits claim on it with 4500.00 give a prior program entitlement of 13500.00; with 52 weeks and a weekly amount of 360.00 (18720.00) the basic maximum benefit amount is 5220.00. Were the prior entitlement 20000.00, the figure would be zero, never negative.
- DUA: a declaration announced on a Wednesday has a 30-day deadline ending on the Friday four weeks and two days later; a claim filed that Friday is timely without good cause.

superseded_clauses: its maximum benefit amount is the lesser of the Extended Benefits fraction times the parent claim's maximum benefit amount (claim_msr_parent_mba) and the maximum duration weeks times the weekly benefit amount plus dependency allowance.
the claimant must show the minimum weeks of full-time base-period employment
